## What This Is

**If you installed any version, apply this.** Two skills return to the Foundation, and the onboarding sequence stops pointing at a file that was not in the box.

`Getting Started/Session 6 - Guided First Pending Plan Implementation.md` is the session that teaches the Pending Plan mechanism. Step 1 told you to open three things: your plan, the governing protocol and `Council Chamber/Skills/Pending Plan Implementation/SKILL.md`. That third file left the Foundation at v2.4.0 and never came back. `Session 4 - Protocol Activation.md` cited it too, in its core Foundation reading list.

So the template shipped the protocol, the PendingPlan object template, the Reconciliation Checklist, three planning protocols and an entire session about implementing plans, while withholding the skill that does the implementing. Two sessions told you to open a file that was not there. It sat that way across eleven releases.

## Why

Two reasons, and the second is the larger one.

**The Foundation is meant to be self-contained.** A skill that every build needs belongs in the box. Most people never visit the public library, and they should not have to in order to finish onboarding. `Pending Plan Implementation` is named by two sessions and backed by a protocol already shipping here. `Researcher` is the parallel-research capability that every build eventually wants and that the template taught nowhere.

**Four documents described the same graduation and gave four different answers.** Ground truth, checked against the skills directory and the published marketplace rather than against prose:

| Surface | Claimed graduated | Claimed dual | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MODULES.md` | five, naming Systematic Debugging | five | both wrong |
| `AGENTS.md` | four | seven | dual stale |
| `README.md` | five | five | both wrong |
| `llms.txt` | five | five | both wrong |
| `Council Chamber/Skills/Skills Index.md` | four | nine | correct |

Systematic Debugging did graduate at v2.4.0, so `MODULES.md` was accurate when it was written. It returned to the Foundation at v3.5.0 and nothing swept the sentence. `AGENTS.md` was corrected at v3.6.0 and the other three were left behind by that same fix.

**The two surfaces that stayed true are the two that refuse to restate a number.** The Skills Index says so in its own text: the list is its own count, so adding a skill leaves no second number to keep in step with it. The `/sovereign-ecosystem` page computes from a released fact rather than repeating it, the fix made at v3.6.0. Every surface that hardcoded a count drifted. Neither surface that derived one did.

A fact restated by hand in a second place will eventually disagree with itself. This release stops restating.

## The Changes

### 1. Two skills return to the Foundation

`Council Chamber/Skills/Pending Plan Implementation/SKILL.md` and `Council Chamber/Skills/Researcher/SKILL.md` now ship here. Both remain installable from the public library for practitioners who run a system of their own. Ships in both homes is the established pattern, set at v3.5.0 when Systematic Debugging and PR Code Review came home the same way.

**Test:** both files exist, and `node "Council Chamber/scripts/build-skills-index.mjs" --check` reports in sync.

### 2. Every skill citation is now checked on every push

`Council Chamber/scripts/check-skill-citations.mjs` is new. It reads every tracked document, finds each backticked citation of the exact shape `Council Chamber/Skills/<Name>/SKILL.md`, and fails if any names a file the repo does not ship. Glob and placeholder forms are skipped, so there is no allowlist to drift.

This class was already findable. `validate-doc-claims.mjs` flags it the moment it is aimed at the file, and nothing ever aimed it. A checker that runs nowhere is indistinguishable from a checker that does not exist.

**Test:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/check-skill-citations.mjs" --positive-control` builds a fixture with one resolving citation, one broken citation and one placeholder, and requires the checker to flag exactly the broken one. Watch it fail before trusting it when it passes. Both the control and the real run are wired into CI.

### 3. Four counts become lists

`MODULES.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and `llms.txt` no longer state how many skills are dual-distribution. They point at the Skills Index, which carries the list. `llms.txt` keeps its enumerations, because an agent reading the manifest uses them, and both are now complete and correct.

**Test:** grep the four files for a spelled or numeric count of dual-distribution skills. There should be none. The Skills Index list is the only place the membership is written.

### 4. Generated link directories stay local

`.claude/skills/` and `.codex/skills/` are now git-ignored. They are symlinks on Mac and Linux and directory junctions on Windows, carrying absolute machine-specific paths that mean nothing in anyone else's clone. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/settings.json` still ship.

Before this, running the documented install step left `?? .claude/skills/` in `git status` permanently, and anyone running `git add -A` committed junctions pointing at their own filesystem.

**Test:** run `node "Council Chamber/scripts/link-skills.mjs"`, then `git status --short`. The link directories should not appear.

### 5. Every citation in the repo now describes something real

A full sweep of backticked `Council Chamber/`, `Getting Started/` and `Vault (Archive)/` paths found 41 that did not resolve. Adjudicated one at a time:

- **13 are patterns**, and correct as written: `Skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `Pending Plans/*.md`, `[Title]`, `{{AI_INTERFACE_NAME}}` and similar. Notation, not citations.
- **22 are destinations created at runtime or by you**: archive targets under `Vault (Archive)/`, `scripts/.env`, `backup.config.json`, `node_modules/`, per-plan support folders. Absent on a fresh clone by design, and accurate as written.
- **6 were misleading**, implying the template shipped something it does not. All six are fixed.

The six:

- **`Council Chamber/AI Interface/AI Interface Change Log.md` now ships.** Four active surfaces read it, the Meta-Governance Audit checks its rollover threshold, and the Skills Governance Protocol requires every skill change to be logged in it. It had never existed. It ships as a starter log matching its siblings in the same directory.
- **Three PowerShell tools are no longer cited.** `Library Vault Eligibility Audit.ps1`, `Pending Plan Reconciliation Sweep.ps1` and `Pending Plans Index Sync.ps1` were named as optional or recommended by four protocol steps and were never in the repo. They were also Windows-only, which no cross-platform template should assume. Each step now describes the work directly and invites you to script it for your own platform if you do it often.
- **The Taste Delta Report template is no longer cited as shipped.** The Universal Taste Calibration Protocol already lists the report's four sections, so the protocol now says to write it plainly and keep your own template if a form settles.
- **`Council Chamber/Templates/Domain Templates/Expression/` and `Council Chamber/Governance/Archetypal Governance Map.md`** are now named as yours to create rather than as shipped surfaces. Domain framing and your archetype map are the parts that cannot be templated.

**Test:** run the sweep yourself. Every remaining non-resolving citation is either a pattern carrying a glob or placeholder character, or a destination the system creates on first use.

## The Migration

**Nothing you have breaks.** This release adds files and corrects prose.

1. Pull v3.12.0.
2. Run `node "Council Chamber/scripts/link-skills.mjs"` so the two returning skills become invocable. A skill on disk with no link is present and unreachable, which is the defect v3.9.0 shipped to fix.
3. Confirm with `node "Council Chamber/scripts/check-skill-mirrors.mjs"`.

**If you already installed either skill from the public library**, you now have two copies: the plugin and the Foundation copy. Keep whichever you prefer and remove the other. They are the same skill. The Foundation copy uses this template's vocabulary and links its sibling protocols directly. The plugin copy carries a Make It Yours section for systems that are not this one.

**If you customized your own Pending Plan Implementation skill**, keep yours. Nothing overwrites it. The linker reports `present` and leaves a real directory alone.

## On the Guard's Narrow Scope

`check-skill-citations.mjs` checks one class: skill citations. It does not check the other 40 paths adjudicated in change 5, because those need judgment that a script cannot carry. A pattern, a runtime destination and a broken reference all look identical to a file-existence test, and telling them apart takes an allowlist.

An allowlist drifts. The moment a guard needs one, it starts reporting clean about entries nobody has re-examined, which is the failure this release exists to fix wearing different clothes. So the shipped guard covers the class where existence is the whole question, and the rest was adjudicated by reading rather than automated by exception.

A broad guard wired to an unadjudicated allowlist would have been a green light attached to nothing.
